claims.text: Substituting Si for Mn in CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of a continuous, coherent protective oxide scale above 900 °C.
The protective scale on the Si-containing alloy is enriched in Cr and Si.
Silicon has sufficiently high oxygen affinity to drive selective formation of the proposed protective scale.
Silicon facilitates formation of a dense mixed oxide such as a Cr-silicate.
The Si-associated mixed oxide has lower metal-cation diffusivity than the oxide on the Mn-containing baseline.
The Si-associated mixed oxide has lower oxygen diffusivity than the oxide on the Mn-containing baseline.
Lower ionic diffusivity in the Si-associated scale reduces growth-induced internal stress.
Stress buildup in an oxide scale can cause the scale to crack and expose the substrate.
Reducing scale stress should reduce cracking and improve scale persistence.
The Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX baseline forms a more porous, less adherent oxide scale that is more susceptible to cracking and spallation.

The Si-containing HEA will retain a stable, coherent oxide during prolonged exposure, whereas the Mn-containing baseline will develop discontinuous, cracked, or spalled oxide under the same conditions.
The proposed Si-versus-Mn behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
The proposed behavior applies in both oxidative and corrosive atmospheres.
The proposed comparison applies over approximately 900–1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The boundary specifies exposure above 900 °C, while the stated conditions and experiment include 900 °C; applicability at exactly 900 °C is therefore inconsistent.
